liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): Reviewer lists Estimated Prophet among the strong second-set pieces, alongside Other One, Wheel and Wharf Rat; Says Jerry's playing reaches new heights across Estimated, He's Gone, short drums, Other One, Wharf Rat and Wheel [12][14]
- **Mississippi Half-Step** (1 review): Half-Step jam is extended at the end, with Billy and Mick making a couple of runs through the drums [16]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Reviewer calls this Peggy-O the most perfect ever [23]
- **Brown-Eyed Women** (1 review): Reviewer calls this Brown-Eyed Women the most smoking ever [23]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the Scarlet into Fire second-set pairing as part of a standout run of songs [12]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Reviewer especially likes Estimated Prophet into He's Gone and the Other One [18]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Music between Other One and Wharf Rat is distinctive, at times with Jerry playing alone [14]

## The recordings

- **gd77-05-25.sbd.shannon.13399.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 178 min; rated 4.61/5 by 88 [1]
- **gd1977-05-25.sbd.shannon.fix-13399.82048.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd1977-05-25.sbd.miller.87591.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 178 min; rated 4.51/5 by 37 [3]. Said about its sound: Small dropout in Wharf Rat fixed, flaws cleaned up and levels adjusted; reel flip between He's Gone and Drums [3]
- **gd1977-05-25.sbd.hamilton.1071.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 179 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [5]. Said about its sound: There is a 0.80-second break at the Scarlet to Fire segue, about two beats [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended at the Mosque, a small hall, with friends; thought the first three songs were the peak [15]
- Reviewer is a lifelong Richmond native, born in 1977, and finds the opening song personally meaningful [19]
- Calls it one of the last shows in the May 1977 run and wonders how Dick's Picks missed it [12]
- Says Peggy-O from St. Paul a couple of weeks earlier was better; also recommends New Haven on the 5th [22]
- Argues the show deserves to be as famous as Cornell, Veneta and Wembley, citing its solid first set [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-05-25.sbd.shannon.13399.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer previously owned this show on DAT; Reviewer calls it a typical Betty Cantor-Jackson soundboard from 1977; Lineage: MR > DAT > CDR > SHN > CDR > SHN [1][16][18]
- **gd1977-05-25.sbd.shannon.fix-13399.82048.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by George Shannon; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: This 2006 version corrects an earlier SHN with sector boundary errors and extra RIFF chunks; tracks resequenced into original order [2]
- **gd1977-05-25.sbd.miller.87591.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> CD D [3]
- **gd1977-05-25.sbd.hamilton.1071.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Seth Kaplan and Greg Hamilton; source: SBD [5]
